changes.reason: The source text of Torah #1 always pairs these two concepts together as a single teaching unit: 'הַחֵן וְהַחֲשִׁיבוּת'. In the dataset they appear as separate nodes connecting to the same targets (מלכות, ספינה, תורה) with identical proof texts — which means they are currently treated as unrelated duplicates rather than as intentionally linked concepts. They are NOT the same thing: חן is grace/charm and חשיבות is importance/esteem. But Rebbe Nachman pairs them deliberately. A direct connection between them would reflect that pairing.
changes.evidence: Source text line 25: 'דְּמַטְבַּע לִסְפִינְתָּא הוּא הַחֵן וְהַחֲשִׁיבוּת, לְשׁוֹן סָפוּן וְחָשׁוּב'. Line 2: 'הַחֵן וְהַחֲשִׁיבוּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִתְעַלֶּה'. The Rebbe never mentions one without the other in this Torah.

changes.reason: The source text (Torah #1, line 26) explicitly equates these two terms in the same sentence: 'וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת צוּצִיתָא דְּנוּרָא חִוַּרְתָּא אֵשׁ לְבָנָה'. The Aramaic phrase 'צוציתא דנורא חורתא' comes from a Talmudic story (Bava Batra 73a) and 'אש לבנה' is its Hebrew translation, provided immediately after by Rebbe Nachman himself. They are the same image: the white tip of a wave that looks like fire — a metaphor for the yetzer hara disguising itself as a mitzvah. This is a translation, not two distinct concepts.
changes.evidence: Source text line 26: 'כִּי מִתְּחִלָּה הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִתְלַבֵּשׁ עַצְמוֹ בְּמִצְווֹת... וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת צוּצִיתָא דְּנוּרָא חִוַּרְתָּא, אֵשׁ לְבָנָה'. The dataset proof for both edges 472 and 473 is identical, confirming they describe the same thing.
